--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.to_undirected()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Convert the graph to an undirected graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.to_undirected()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Convert the graph to an undirected graph. title: >- [Graph.to_undirected()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Convert the graph to an undirected graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Convert the graph to an undirected graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L37957-L38049){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.to_undirected() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Convert to undirected](../assets/graphs/to-undirected.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A directed graph with a mutual pair of accent arrows between A and B, plus arrows A to D and D to C. After to_undirected(), the mutual pair collapses into a single accent edge A to B, and the other two edges simply lose their arrowheads." width="100%"} Creates a new graph with the same nodes and edges, but without edge direction. If the graph is already undirected, returns a new copy. For directed graphs, converts directed edges to undirected edges, removing duplicate pairs. Many analyses are defined only for undirected graphs (cliques, the leading-eigenvector and other community methods, most clustering measures), and many relationships are better treated as mutual even when the data records a direction. Converting is the usual way to: - run undirected-only algorithms on directed data (e.g., `find_cliques()` or `cmty_l_eigenvec()`) - treat a one-way relation such as "follows", "cites", or "emails" as plain "connected to" - study weak connectivity, where direction does not matter Node IDs, labels, and node attributes are carried over unchanged. Every directed edge becomes an undirected edge with its weight and attributes. When both `A -> B` and `B -> A` exist, only the first one added is kept, so the weight and attributes of the reverse edge are discarded rather than combined. Node and kept edge IDs are the same as in the original. The original graph is not modified. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new undirected Graph with the same nodes and edges (with mutual directed pairs merged into single edges). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A directed triangle becomes an undirected one: ::: {#dc475157 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec directed = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) undirected = directed.to_undirected() undirected.is_directed() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Since each of the three original edges connects a unique pair, converting to undirected doesn't collapse any of them: ::: {#66f5aff5 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} undirected.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Mutual edges are a different story. "Alice" and "Bob" follow each other, so their two directed edges collapse into one undirected connection, and three directed edges become two undirected ones: ::: {#72d3d71c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} followers = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"]) .add_edges([("Alice", "Bob"), ("Bob", "Alice"), ("Bob", "Charlie")]) ) connections = followers.to_undirected() connections.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['Alice--Bob', 'Bob--Charlie'] ``` ::: ::: When a mutual pair is merged, the edge added first wins. Here the `A -> B` edge (weight `2.0`) is kept and the `B -> A` edge (weight `5.0`) is dropped: ::: {#82381948 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} weighted = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge("A", "B", weight=2.0) .add_edge("B", "A", weight=5.0) ) weighted.to_undirected().get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
